title: Unified Firebase app with role-based access, global header/profile menu, and in-app admin dashboard

requirements.text: Align the Firestore user document schema to exactly `users/{uid}` with fields: `name` (string), `email` (string), `photoURL` (string), `role` ("user" | "admin" | "super_admin"), `approved` (boolean), and `createdAt` (Firestore timestamp). Ensure signup writes these fields and that subsequent profile reads in the app use these fields.

quotes:
Firestore users collection:
- Store every user in users/{uid}
- Fields:
  name (string)
  email (string)
  photoURL (string)
  role ("user" | "admin" | "super_admin")
  approved (boolean)
  createdAt (timestamp)

acceptanceCriteria: After signup, the Firestore document at `users/{uid}` exists and contains `name`, `email`, `photoURL`, `role`, `approved`, and `createdAt` (as a Firestore Timestamp, e.g., via `serverTimestamp()`), with no dependency on additional required fields.
Login gating continues to rely on the boolean `approved === true` from a fresh server read.
The app can display the logged-in user’s `name`, `role`, and `photoURL` using the new schema.

requirements.text: Implement the first-ever signup rule: when the users collection has no users, the first created account must be assigned `role = "super_admin"` and `approved = true`; all subsequent signups must be assigned `role = "user"` and `approved = false`.

quotes:
On first-ever signup, automatically assign:
  role = "super_admin"
  approved = true

acceptanceCriteria: When the users collection is empty, the first signup creates `users/{uid}` with `role="super_admin"` and `approved=true`.
When at least one user exists, a new signup creates `users/{uid}` with `role="user"` and `approved=false`.

requirements.text: Add a global header that is displayed on all pages in the single app. Header layout: left side shows app logo + app name; right side shows the current user’s profile picture (clickable) when authenticated.

quotes:
Header:
- Show a global header on all pages.
- Left: app logo + app name
- Right: user profile picture (clickable)

acceptanceCriteria: All routes/screens render the same header at the top of the viewport.
Header left renders an app logo image asset and an app name string.
When a user is logged in, the header right renders their `photoURL` as an avatar button; when logged out, the avatar area is hidden or replaced with a neutral placeholder (no errors).

requirements.text: Implement the profile popup opened by clicking the header avatar. The popup must always show the user’s name and role. If the role is `admin` or `super_admin`, also show an "Open Admin Dashboard" button. Always show a "Logout" button that signs the user out and returns them to the login screen.

quotes:
Profile popup:
- On clicking profile picture, open a popup.
- Always show name + role.
- If role is admin or super_admin, show:
  "Open Admin Dashboard" button
- Always show Logout button.

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking the avatar opens a popup/menu anchored to the avatar button.
Popup contains visible text for the user `name` and `role`.
For `role in {admin, super_admin}`, popup shows a button labeled exactly "Open Admin Dashboard" that navigates to the admin area.
Popup always includes a "Logout" button that signs out and navigates to `/login`.

requirements.text: Add an in-app Admin Dashboard area within the same application (no separate admin app). Access must be restricted to users whose Firestore role is `admin` or `super_admin`. Include the following pages/sections: Dashboard (stats), Users list, Chats, Reports, Settings.

quotes:
Admin Dashboard:
- Accessible only if role is admin or super_admin.
- Pages:
  - Dashboard (stats)
  - Users list
  - Chats
  - Reports
  - Settings

UI:
- No separate admin app

Build everything inside one single application.

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to an admin route while not `admin`/`super_admin` redirects back to the non-admin area (e.g., `/home`) and does not render admin content.
Admin Dashboard includes navigation to the 5 required pages/sections within the same SPA.
Dashboard page shows basic stats placeholders derived from Firestore where feasible (e.g., total users, approved users, pending users).
Chats/Reports/Settings pages can be UI placeholders but must exist and be reachable via the admin navigation.

requirements.text: Implement the Users list page in the Admin Dashboard that lists all user documents from `users` (including `super_admin` users) and supports user management actions with role-based permissions: Admins can approve users, block users, and change role between `user` and `admin`. Super admins can do all admin actions and can promote users to admin. Enforce that "super_admin is also a normal user with extra permissions" and appears in the user list.

quotes:
User behavior:
- All users including super_admin must appear in the user list.
- Super admin is also a normal user with extra permissions.

User Management:
- Admin can:
  - Approve users
  - Block users
  - Change role (user ↔ admin)
- Super admin can:
  - Do everything admin can
  - Promote users to admin

acceptanceCriteria: Users list shows all users in the `users` collection (admins and super_admins included).
Approve action updates the selected user document such that they can log in (i.e., `approved` becomes `true`).
Block action updates the selected user such that they cannot log in anymore (e.g., `approved` becomes `false`), and the UI reflects the blocked/unapproved state.
Role change action allows toggling `role` between `user` and `admin` for non-super_admin users according to the current operator’s permissions.
The UI prevents changing any user to `super_admin` via the dashboard and prevents demoting a `super_admin` user via the dashboard.

requirements.text: Update Firestore security rules to enforce the role-based permissions required by the admin dashboard and user management, while keeping regular users limited to reading/updating only their own profile (excluding role/approved changes). Ensure admins can read all users for listing. Ensure rules restrict any attempt to set `role` to `super_admin` via client writes and restrict modifications to existing `super_admin` users’ roles/approval by non-super_admins.

quotes:
Accessible only if role is admin or super_admin.
...
User Management:
- Admin can:
  - Approve users
  - Block users
  - Change role (user ↔ admin)
- Super admin can:
  - Do everything admin can
  - Promote users to admin

acceptanceCriteria: A non-admin authenticated user can read only `users/{auth.uid}` and cannot update `role` or `approved`.
An admin/super_admin can read all documents in `users` (required for the user list).
Client writes that attempt to create/update any document with `role == "super_admin"` are denied by Firestore rules (except for the first-user creation flow if supported by current rule strategy).
Updates to an existing `super_admin` user’s `role`/`approved` are rejected unless the requester is `super_admin`.

requirements.text: Apply a clean, WhatsApp-style, mobile-friendly UI across the unified app (auth screens, header, home, and admin dashboard) with consistent spacing, typography, and a green-forward palette (avoid blue/purple). Keep all user-facing text in English.

quotes:
UI:
- Clean, WhatsApp-style simple UI
- Mobile-friendly

Use English for any user-facing text in the build request.

acceptanceCriteria: Primary navigation and key actions are easily usable on mobile widths (~360px) without horizontal scrolling.
Admin Dashboard navigation is usable on mobile (e.g., collapsible sidebar, tabs, or a responsive drawer).
All visible UI strings are in English.
Visual styling is consistent across screens and matches a simple WhatsApp-like aesthetic.

requirements.text: Add a static app logo image asset and render it in the global header next to the app name.

quotes:
Header:
- Left: app logo + app name

acceptanceCriteria: A logo file exists under `frontend/public/assets/generated/` and is used in the header.
Logo renders crisply at typical header sizes (~24–32px) on light and dark backgrounds.

constraints: Do not edit files under `frontend/src/components/ui` (compose them instead).
Do not modify immutable hook paths: `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx`, `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`.
Keep the application as a single unified React app (no separate admin application).
Backend must remain single-actor if modified; only introduce `backend/migration.mo` if state migration is required.
nonGoals: Implementing realtime chat or WebSocket-based messaging for the Chats page (UI placeholder is sufficient).
Integrating Firebase Storage or any external file storage for avatars (store `photoURL` as a string per requirements; it may be a data URL if needed).
Adding third-party authentication providers beyond Firebase Auth email/password.
Implementing push notifications, email sending, or external admin tooling.

required: Flat chat-bubble logo icon with a simple green palette on transparent background (app-logo.dim_256x256.png)
